recent_posts.title: The Computer Is Personal Again
recent_posts.summary: Perplexity's Personal Computer is analyzed as a new 'control layer' rather than just another app — an agentic system that orchestrates 19 models, accesses local Mac files and apps, and executes multi-step tasks like processing receipts, managing paperwork, and automating household admin. The piece frames this as a shift from direct manipulation computing to delegation-based computing, where trust, permissions, and audit trails become the new OS primitives. It compares Perplexity's managed-cloud approach to OpenClaw's self-hosted alternative, notes the Samsung Galaxy S26 integration as a distribution signal, and cautions against believing unverified ROI claims or privacy assumptions. The killer use case is argued to be mundane life admin — the 'connective tissue between tasks' — rather than glamorous AI workflows.

recent_posts.title: Lightricks open-sources LTX-2 video model in a Linux-style ecosystem play
recent_posts.summary: Lightricks released LTX-2, a fully open-source AI video model (Apache 2.0) with 14B video and 5B audio parameters that co-evolve during generation, enabling native 4K output at up to 50fps on consumer GPUs like an RTX 3060. Unlike Sora, Veo, and Runway, Lightricks published full model weights, training code, inference code, and LoRA trainer. LTX-2.3 also ships with a free local desktop app. While ranked #36 on quality leaderboards, it costs $3.60/min vs Sora's $30/min, uses licensed Getty/Shutterstock training data for enterprise compliance, and has 5M downloads in under 3 months. The strategic play mirrors Linux: build an open ecosystem with developer community momentum, fine-tuning capabilities, and a platform (LTX Studio) that integrates multiple models, betting that openness and ecosystem growth outpace closed competitors long-term.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Supercut a new high-quality screen recording tool
recent_posts.summary: Supercut, a new screen recording tool, is positioned as a superior alternative to Loom. Built by the team behind Typeform, Supercut focuses on speed, quality, and design from the ground up. It offers features such as easy audio cleanup, chaptering, captioning, and video downloads. The tool is enhanced by AI functionalities aimed at improving user experience. Supercut is currently available for free during its Open Beta phase.

recent_posts.title: Theater of Power and the Cost of Stupidity
recent_posts.summary: The author discusses the transformative period we are living in, highlighting the advancements in AI, fusion energy, and space exploration. However, he criticizes current global leadership for being bogged down by old conflicts and petty divisions rather than focusing on these advancements. He argues that the path to peace is straightforward but often ignored due to power struggles and outdated thinking. The author calls for unity and forward-thinking to tackle bigger issues like climate change and artificial superintelligence.

recent_posts.title: The Age of (humanoid) Robots
recent_posts.summary: The age of humanoid robots is upon us, driven by the current AI revolution. Companies like Honda and Boston Dynamics have made significant advancements in this field. The new Atlas robot from Boston Dynamics has impressive abilities, including an omnidirectional upper torso, legs, and head. The robotics industry is getting better at understanding the world, interacting with humans, and becoming more affordable to manufacture at scale.
